applied.quote: A 100% Roth 401(k) saver can therefore build a Traditional balance from the match, and that pre-tax match is taxed when withdrawn in retirement.
applied.replacement: A 100% Roth 401(k) saver can therefore build a Traditional balance from the match.
applied.why: SOURCE says nothing about how the match is taxed at withdrawal

applied.quote: It is not a reason to avoid Roth deferrals.
applied.why: SOURCE makes no evaluation of whether to avoid Roth deferrals

applied.quote: Only vested match money qualifies, and a Roth match counts as taxable income in the year it is allocated to your account.
applied.replacement: Only vested match money qualifies, and a Roth match is not excludable from your gross income.
applied.why: SOURCE says not excludable from gross income; gives no timing

applied.quote: Whether a plan offers a Roth match is written into its plan document.
applied.replacement: To see whether your plan offers a Roth match, check the plan document.
applied.why: SOURCE does not say where a plan records the Roth match option

applied.quote: Pre-tax by default; since SECURE 2.0, a plan may offer vested match as Roth, taxed in the year allocated
applied.replacement: Pre-tax by default; since SECURE 2.0, a plan may offer vested match as Roth, not excludable from gross income
applied.why: SOURCE gives no year-allocated timing, only not excludable from income
